note: Muscatine County Conservation recreation area on the Cedar River about eight miles northwest of Muscatine, named for the old bridge whose last two spans now carry foot traffic. The Main Campground sits in the woods near the lodge with a campground host and playground; the River Campground is a separate loop on the river bank about 500 m west. Boat ramps on the Cedar River and Chicken Creek, canoe and kayak rental, hiking and equestrian trails. --Claude
summary: County pages confirm 24 electric (20/30/50A) Main Campground sites with 62-ft pads at $25 and reservable online, 9 non-electric River Campground spurs at $20 FCFS, $10 hike-in tent area, showers, flush and vault toilets, water, dump, 14-day limit, April 15 to October 31. No split: the two campgrounds are ~500 m apart. Not waterfront kept for the main campground; the river loop is a possible riverview I could not confirm.
flags: BOOKING CONFLICT on the operator's own page: the camping activity page's Overview says of the Main Campground 'Campsites are available on a first-come, first-served basis only. No reservations are taken.', but the same page's Fees say 'Reserve Sites Online starting April 15, 2025', and sites 001-024 are live bookable facilities on mycountyparks ('This is a reservable, electric only site'). Written as reservable with fcfs some_sites; the Overview text looks stale.

SPLIT CHECK: no split. On the county park map (saulsbury_map_16691.jpg) and NAIP, the Main Campground loop (pin, 41.4982,-91.1693) and the River Campground loop (bank road, ~41.4970,-91.1750) are about 500 m apart, under the ~1 km line. The river loop is reached by its own short park road off the same park entrance from Saulsbury Road, and it shares the main campground's showers ('Showers available in Main Campground').

WATERFRONT: 'not waterfront' kept. The Main Campground (the pin and all 24 electric sites) is in floodplain woods ~110 m from the Chicken Creek backwater, with the park road and a tree belt between, and ~450 m from the Cedar River. The River Campground's 9 non-electric spurs line a road on the Cedar River bank (river ~150 m wide), and the county says 'no electricity but great river view'. But on NAIP a continuous strip of bank trees, 10-20 m deep, runs between that road and the water, and I found no official photo of a river site (the gallery's river photo is the boat ramp). The river spurs' fit for a 23-ft rig is also unstated, so I could not confirm riverview and applied the downgrade rule. A dated photo of a river site would settle it.
FEES BASE: the $20 low is the River Campground spur. It is drive-in with 'on-site parking', but no pad size is published for it; if it doesn't fit a 23-ft rig, the base is $25.
PIN: stored 41.49822,-91.16925 is inside the Main Campground loop. OK.
